items.label: section_header
items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: When asked about a homologous series in the exam, it is probably best to only write about the properties (the second and third bullet points). Sometimes you do not get separate marks for 'the same functional group' and 'similar chemical properties', and perhaps a better way of writing this is 'they have similar chemical properties because they have the same functional group'.

items.label: section_header
items.text: MEMBERS OF A HOMOLOGOUS SERIES HAVE THE SAME GENERAL FORMULA

items.label: section_header
items.text: ISOMERS OF ALKANES

items.label: text
items.text: Isomers are compounds which have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae. The alkanes shown in Table 24.1 can all be described as straight-chain alkanes or as having an unbranched chain. There are also isomers of butane and pentane that have branched chains. These are shown in Figure 24.2.

items.label: section_header
items.text: HOMOLOGOUS SERIES

items.label: text
items.text: The alkanes form a homologous series. A homologous series is a series of compounds that:

items.label: list_item
items.text: have the same functional group

items.label: list_item
items.text: have similar chemical properties

items.label: list_item
items.text: show a trend (gradation)in physical properties

items.label: list_item
items.text: can be described by the same general formula

items.label: list_item
items.text: differ from the next by a -CH2- unit.

items.label: text
items.text: The alkanes form the simplest homologous series. The alkanes do not really havi  i h ih  s n    ui a  ich are the basis of all other organic compounds.

items.label: text
items.text: In the case of the alkanes, if there are n carbons, there are 2n + 2 hydrogens.

items.label: text
items.text: The general formula for the alkanes is CH2n+2.

items.label: text
items.text: So, for example, if there are three carbons, there are (2 × 3) + 2 = 8 hydrogens. The formula for propane is C3H8.

items.label: text
items.text: If you want the formula for an alkane with 15 carbons, you could work out that it is C15H32and so on.

items.label: text
items.text: The reason that the alkanes and other homologous series can be described by a general formula is that each member differs from the next by a -CH2—unit.
